notes: John C. Calhoun was re-elected vice president with 171 electoral votes, while 7 electors voted for William Smith.
In Delaware and South Carolina the legislature chose the electors, so those states had no popular vote.

Maryland and Tennessee chose their electors by district, and Maine chose two statewide and the rest by district. New York chose one elector per district, and those electors then chose the remaining two.
Maine, Maryland and New York split their electoral votes.
In Georgia two rival slates of Jackson electors ran, one from the Troup faction and one from the Clark faction. Both slates’ votes are counted for Jackson.

Added up state by state, Jackson has 641,320 votes and Adams 500,722, close to the American Presidency Project’s 642,553 and 500,897. Wikipedia’s national table gives Jackson 638,348 and Adams 507,440, and lists the Clark slate’s 7,991 Georgia votes on a separate line.
